Oops! It seems that there was an error while retrieving the scientific articles related to the experiment. Let me try again.

In the meantime, I can provide you with the materials and procedure for the egg drop experiment, as well as safety precautions.

Materials:
1. Raw eggs
2. Various materials for building the protective devices (e.g., cardboard, bubble wrap, straws, rubber bands, tape, cotton balls, etc.)
3. Measuring tape or ruler
4. Markers or labels for identifying each device

Procedure:
1. Divide the students into groups.
2. Explain the objective of the experiment: to design a protective device that will prevent an egg from breaking when dropped from a specified height.
3. Provide the materials to each group.
4. Instruct the students to brainstorm and design a protective device using the materials provided. They should consider factors such as size, weight, and materials used in their design.
5. Once the devices are constructed, assign each group a number or label to identify their device.
6. Set a designated height from which all devices will be dropped (e.g., 2 meters).
7. Have each group carefully place their egg inside the protective device.
8. Line up all the devices at the dropping point.
9. One by one, drop each device from the designated height.
10. After each drop, examine the condition of the egg inside the device and record the results (e.g., intact, cracked, or broken).
11. Discuss the results as a class and ask the students to analyze why some devices were more successful than others.
12. Encourage the students to modify their designs and repeat the experiment to improve the results.

Safety Precautions:
1. Ensure that the dropping area is clear of any obstacles.
2. Make sure that students wear safety goggles and handle the materials and devices with care.
3. Caution students to avoid any sudden movements during the experiment.
4. Provide adult supervision to ensure safety throughout the experiment.

I apologize for the inconvenience regarding the scientific articles. Let me try to retrieve them again.
